newsitem.title: USA: US DOE offers draft plan to move reactor waste.
newsitem.headline: US DOE offers draft plan to move reactor waste.

text.p: The U.S. Energy Department Monday offered a draft proposal for private firms to accept and transport waste from civilian nuclear reactors.

The department will take comments until March 31, 1997, on the proposal for private contractors in a project expected to last 40 years to move spent nuclear reactor fuel from current storage at utilities' reactors across the country to a designated government facility.
The department, which becomes responsible for spent fuel from utilities' reactors next year, still does not have a designated repository site for the waste.

The department's draft plan uses a three-stage approach. In the first one-year phase, contractors would develop plans to accept and transport spent nuclear fuel and to deliver storage containers to a federal facility.
Under the second eight-year phase, contractors would complete preparations, including developing necessary equipment, facilities and storage equipment.
The third phase, which is to last five years, puts the contractor's plan into operation and hinges on the Energy Department opening a repository or receiving facilities.

The plan separates the country into four service regions, and bidders would submit proposals to service each region in the first phase. The department expects to award one or more contracts under a cost-sharing plan for that phase.
In the second phase, accepted contractors would be eligible to proceed for up to two regions. Contractors' costs during that time would be recovered in the final phase, the department said.
The overall waste acceptance, transportation and storage project is expected to last about 40 years, and the department said it expected to seek more competitive proposals during that time.
